ideas: A real weakness that matters but doesn't break the job
A specific example of when it caused a problem
What you're doing about it and the progress so far

phrases.meaning: I usually do something, often a habit
I have been improving something over time
say what you think, especially in a group

learn.explain: The interviewer is testing self-awareness and honesty, not looking for a reason to reject you. Fake weaknesses like "I'm a perfectionist" or "I work too hard" lose trust immediately. Choose a real weakness that is not a core requirement of the job (for an FDE, don't say "I can't explain things" or "I don't like customers"), give a short specific example of when it caused a problem, and spend most of the answer on what you're doing about it and the evidence that it's improving. Good options for a new graduate: not asking for help early enough, hesitating to speak up in meetings, over-polishing before sharing work, or underestimating tasks.
points: It's a real weakness, with a specific example.
It isn't a core requirement of the role.
Most of the answer is about the improvement plan and the progress.
mistakes: Fake weaknesses: "I'm a perfectionist", "I care too much".
A weakness that disqualifies you for the role.
Describing the weakness for a long time and the improvement in one sentence.

framework.starter: To be honest, I tend to…
So what I've been working on is…
It's still a work in progress, but…

betterWays.weak: My weakness is I am perfectionist.
betterWays.strong: To be honest, I tend to wait too long before asking for help.
Like everyone, I have a few. The one I'm working on most right now is…

betterWays.weak: I am not good at English.
betterWays.strong: My spoken English is less fluent than my written English, so I practise speaking every day with recorded sessions.
betterWays.why: Honest, specific, and shows a concrete plan.

betterWays.strong: Now I set myself a rule: if I'm stuck for more than an hour, I ask, with notes on what I've tried.
betterWays.why: A specific habit is more credible than "I fixed it".

betterWays.weak: It is not a problem anymore.
betterWays.strong: It's still a work in progress, but my lead noticed the difference in my last two months.
betterWays.why: Honest about ongoing effort, with evidence.

model: To be honest, I tend to wait too long before asking for help. I think it comes from wanting to prove I can solve things myself, especially as the most junior person. The situation was in my internship. I was stuck on a bug in the data import for almost two days. I didn't want to bother anyone, so I kept trying things on my own. When I finally asked a senior engineer, she found the problem in about twenty minutes: a configuration setting I didn't even know existed. As a result, the feature was a day late, and that was completely avoidable. That made me realise that waiting isn't independence; it just costs the team time. So what I did was set myself a simple rule: if I'm stuck for more than an hour, I ask. And when I ask, I bring short notes on what I've already tried, so I'm not wasting the other person's time. I've also been working on being the one who speaks up first in stand-ups when something is blocked. It's still a work in progress, but by the end of the internship, my lead mentioned that I was flagging problems much earlier. For an FDE role, where you're often working alone at a customer, I think that habit matters even more.
short: To be honest, I tend to wait too long before asking for help. In my internship, I spent two days on a bug that a senior engineer solved in twenty minutes, and the feature was late. Now I have a rule: stuck for an hour, I ask, and I bring notes on what I've tried. It's still a work in progress, but my lead noticed I was flagging problems much earlier.

followUps.q: Isn't asking for help a lot a problem too?
followUps.answer: Yes, it can be, which is why I try a few things first and bring notes. The goal isn't to ask more; it's to ask at the right time, with the work already done, so the conversation is short and useful.

followUps.q: What other weaknesses do you have?
followUps.answer: My spoken English is less fluent than my written English, especially under pressure. I practise every day by recording myself explaining technical topics, and I'm noticeably more comfortable than six months ago.

followUps.q: How would this weakness show up at a customer site?
followUps.answer: It could mean a customer waiting longer than necessary. That's exactly why I want to fix it before I'm in that situation. At a customer, my one-hour rule would probably be even shorter.

selfCheck: The weakness was real, not a disguised strength.
I gave a specific example with a consequence.
Most of my answer was about improvement.
I answered the follow-up without restarting a sentence.
